title: Release Ballet: cadence checklist and ops diary (Jun 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working draft of the release 'ballet' for the Jun 22–26 mini-rollout. Intended as a compact operator checklist + annotated diary for the shift crew. Use this to run preflight, holdback, canary, and ramp phases with clear signal & rollback triggers.

Context / scope:
- Release artifact: serving-runtime v2.11.3 (binary + kernel selection changes; improved batching heuristics).
- Target lanes: hosted-api (primary), dedicated (gradual), private (no-auto deploy).
- Audience: release conductor, shift operators, on-call SRE, product owner.
- Primary goals: 1) validate latency SLO across p95/p99 under staging-like traffic; 2) verify KV-cache warmup behavior; 3) confirm fallback routing works when quantized-variant capacity is low.

High-level calendar (Ballet acts):
- Act I — Preflight (Mon Jun 22)
  - 09:00: kick-off: quick stand (15m) — attendees: conductor, infra lead, SRE on-call, two operators, product owner.
  - 09:15–11:00: environment checks (see preflight checklist).
  - 11:00–13:00: smoke deploy to staging lane + smoke-suite run (10% traffic simulator).
  - 14:00: decision gate: if smoke failures > 2 tests OR p99 latency bump > 40% -> abort and revert staging -> open postmortem RFI (ENG-3421).

- Act II — Micro-canary (Tue Jun 23)
  - 08:00: deploy to canary pool (1% traffic hosted-api).
  - 08:30–12:00: continuous sampling — telemetry flagged; ops keep watchlist.
  - 12:00: intermediate puppet-check and heartbeat call (5m). If any customer-facing errors appear, escalate immediately.
  - 15:00: canary expansion decision: pass -> 5% -> proceed to Act III; fail -> rollback to previous model/kernel.

- Act III — Gradual roll (Wed Jun 24)
  - 07:00: 5% -> 25% ramp window with 45 minute stabilization between steps.
  - 13:00: 25% -> 60% (only if signal is clean).
  - 18:00: optional evening hold; night ops on-call takes watch.

- Act IV — Full release / closure (Thu Jun 25)
  - 09:00: final 100% push for hosted-api if telemetry green for >12h after 60% ramp.
  - 12:00: publish release notes draft to #deploys and product release doc.
  - 16:00: retrospective notes in this doc; mark follow-ups.

Preflight checklist (Act I detailed):
- infra/alloc: confirm N+2 GPU pool health for canary nodes (check node-exporter + GPU exporter).
- config: deploy manifest hash and config diff (git tag + PR-609).
- key roll: KMS access token rotation was tested in staging (ticket: ENG-3390).
- feature flags: ensure canary-flag is on for routing-service (ff: serving_runtime_canary).
- smoke tests: run 12 smoke scenarios (list below), record pass/fail and response traces.
- perf baseline: snapshot p50/p95/p99 and token throughput for baseline version (v2.11.2) for comparison.
- telemetry sanity: ensure dashboards exist and alerts disabled for expected noise; set temporary alert thresholds to avoid noisy paging during ramp.

Smoke suite (select):
- small-response generation (seq_len 64)
- long-context generation (seq_len 2048)
- streaming response stability (partial cancel)
- embeddings consistency (sample corpus)
- fallback routing: simulate quantized-variant OOM and confirm routing to non-quantized variant.
- KV-cache warmup: measure first-request and warm-request latency.

Operator watchlist (signals to track in real-time):
- Latency: p95 > baseline * 1.3 OR p99 > baseline * 1.5 -> immediate rollback consideration.
- Error rate: new 5xx count > 0.2% of requests in a 5m window -> investigate.
- Token cost delta: >+12% unit cost over expected for 30m -> investigate batching change.
- Queue growth: worker queue length rising > 50% -> throttle or scale.
- Memory OOMs: any new OOM patterns -> kill roll and revert.

Quick rollback matrix (who pulls the cord):
- Auto-rollback trigger (immediate): p99 above threshold for 10m AND error rate spike > 0.5% -> system should pause expansion and revert canary via automation.
- Operator-initiated rollback: SRE on-call or infra lead must approve and execute rollback; conductor records the reason in this doc and in ENG ticket.
- Product hold: product owner can instruct a manual hold (no further expansion) if user-impacting issues observed.

Communication templates (post to #deploys and customer-facing brief):
- Internal short (Slack): "deploy: serving-runtime v2.11.3 -> canary(1%). Smoke pass. Watch p99/p95 and 5xx. Conductor: Maya T. On-call: Ethan P. Decision window 15:00 UTC."
- Customer blurb (release notes draft): "We rolled out serving-runtime v2.11.3 — improvements to batching and latency for short-path generation. No expected API changes. Please file issues to support@redwood.ai if you see regressions. See changelog: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/releases/tag/v2.11.3"

Night-shift / after-hours guidance:
- If evening expansion is scheduled, transfer conductor duties to on-call engineer at 18:00 with a 1:1 handoff.
- Leave a short ops diary entry in this doc for each handover (time + state + any open investigation).

Telemetry queries & dashboards (starter snippets):
- p99 latency (hosted-api): "sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{le=\"0.99\"}[5m]))" (ops: tune to local PromQL naming).
- 5xx rate: "increase(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\"}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total[5m])"
- queue length: "gauge serving_queue_length{name=\"runtime-worker\"}"
- memory OOMs: process_ooms_total by node

Debrief / release notes draft (to be refined post closure):
- Key changes:
  - Kernel selection optimizer: chooses faster matmul path for seq_len<128. Expected median p50 improvements 6–9% for short generation.
  - Batching heuristic tweak: prefers shorter-latency windows; could increase token cost in low-batch environments.
  - KV-cache bugfix: fixed race during cache eviction on heavy parallel reads.
- Known issues / watch items:
  - Observed slight p99 bump on a subset of warmup-heavy queries (investigating).
  - Unit token cost may increase for low-concurrency traffic until batching equilibrates.
- Rollout status: staged canary -> planned expansion (see calendar above).

Follow-ups / action items post-release (owners):
- eng/perf: analyze warmup p99 (owner: Priya Nair, ENG-3457).
- infra: add an automated KV-cache smoke in nightly CI (owner: Liam O'Connor).
- docs: update release notes and changelog (owner: Maya Thompson).

Notes-to-self (rough):
- keep the "ballet" metaphor — it helps the crew think in acts and cues rather than only numbers.
- consider a short canned runbook for model-routing fallback — put behind a quick button in the console for next sprint.

Operator diary entries (examples):
- 2026-06-22 09:36 — Maya T: Preflight complete. Smoke run: 12/12 pass. Baseline p99 +4% vs v2.11.2 (within expected).
- 2026-06-23 08:45 — Ethan P: Canary up (1%). Observed two transient 503s tied to ephemeral node reboots in AZ-us-west-2a. Auto-restarted node group; no customer impact.
- 2026-06-24 14:10 — Priya N: 25% -> 60% expansion paused for 30m due to p95 spike in a specific shard. Investigating heatmap; tied to cache warming. Decision: continue after 45m hold with scaled-up worker pool.

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Does the batching heuristic change require a permanent tweak to per-tenant batch windows? (Discuss with product and perf).
- Should we expose a per-tenant cap to avoid cost regressions for very low throughput tenants?

Attachments / artifacts to attach to final release note:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/609
- Perf comparison table (CSV) — upload to the release folder after perf job completes.
- Smoke-run logs: staging/smoke/2026-06-22/logs.tar.gz (ops artifact).

If anything in this doc is ambiguous, ping me (Maya) or drop the phrase "release ballet" in #deploys and I will call a quick 1:1 decision.

-- end of working draft --
